question: On 19 November 2025, the Belgium-based Hind Rajab Foundation (HRF)1 released a statement that ‘on 22 October, Europol invited HRF to speak at its annual meeting in The Hague. This invitation forms part of a broader communication process and an exploration of possible cooperation between HRF and Europol.

’ In response to a non-governmental organisation monitor inquiry, Europol stated that it ‘is maintaining and exploring cooperation with a number of stakeholders, including civil society organisations that collect and document alleged war crimes around the world,’ adding that ‘Europol has also been in contact with HRF.

’ The HRF is anonymously funded and chaired by Dyab Abou Jahjah2, who has publicly admitted past involvement with Hezbollah (including its military wing), has been identified as linked to several actors designated as part of Hezbollah’s vast terror funding network, and has a documented record of violent and antisemitic statements3.
In the light of Europol’s acknowledged contact with the HRF, could the Commission clarify: 1.
whether protocols are in place to screen third parties that work with Europol for affiliation with terrorist entities, in accordance with counterterrorism measures?
whether, in the light of these events, the Commission will require Europol to suspend its cooperation with the HRF?
answer: Pursuant to Article 88 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (1), Europol’s mission is to support competent authorities of the Member States in their investigations on serious cross-border crime, terrorism and forms of crime which affect a common interest covered by the EU policy.

Genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes are among the forms of crime for which Europol supports Member States, in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/794 (2). To pursue this mission, in 2018 Europol established a dedicated Analysis Project (3) on Core International Crimes.

While Europol does not initiate investigations, it provides support to Member States’ investigations under a robust data protection framework. In fulfilling this mission to support Member States investigations, Europol engages with numerous stakeholders and private parties, academia and civil society organisations.

This includes engaging with representatives from non-governmental organisations and media involved with investigating and documenting genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity globally. According to information received from Europol, the meeting with the Hind Rajab Foundation took place in the context of Europol’s support as regards Core International Crimes.

The contact with the Hind Rajab Foundation was exploratory. This meeting was preceded by an assessment on the nature and activities of the Hind Rajab Foundation. Europol has not engaged in further contacts with this foundation.
